videos.title: Your path in the Academy in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Your path in the MoRo Academy. Seven levels, from awareness to master instructor. L1 Awareness: anyone on the floor. L2 Operator, then L3A Technician or L3B Programmer. L4A Systems Engineer or L4B Advanced Programmer. L5 Master Instructor trains others. From L2 up, you also show it in practice.

videos.title: Meet MoRo in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Meet MoRo. MoRo is an autonomous mobile robot. It moves loads around your floor, on its own. No tape and no magnets on the floor. It maps the room with LiDAR, so it can work out where it is. Three models: A-250, A-500 and A-1200. Same navigation. Different payloads: 250, 500 and 1,200 kg. On screen at the end: Next: what MoRo is in more detail. MoRo Academy, DiFacto Robotics & Automation.

videos.title: Three models, three jobs in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Three models, three jobs. The A-250 carries up to 250 kg, and moves faster. It suits light assembly and small-item transport. The A-500 carries up to 500 kg. It is the most deployed, for machine tending. The A-1200 carries up to 1,200 kg, and moves slower. It suits heavy transfer and forklift replacement.

videos.title: Maps, not tape in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Maps, not tape. How MoRo finds its way. LiDAR measures distance with laser light. It sees walls, machines, pillars and people. SLAM locates MoRo and builds the map at once. So no floor tape or magnets are needed. Glass and mirror-like surfaces can confuse LiDAR. If the layout changes, the map needs updating.

videos.title: Meet the control interface in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The control interface, in 30 seconds. MoRo is managed through software: the HMI. On MoRo, it is called ANT. You do not need a technical background. Most of the time, you supervise. You observe and confirm actions. You step in only when needed.

videos.title: The startup sequence in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The startup sequence, in 30 seconds. First, a visual check: path clear, sensors unobstructed. Then power on: MoRo runs its own diagnostic. It checks battery, navigation and safety systems. Wait for the ready state. Only then assign a mission. Assigning early: a common cause of interrupted starts.

videos.title: Manual override and E-stop in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Manual override and E-stop, in 30 seconds. MoRo works autonomously by default. Override: setup repositioning, a blocked path, post-maintenance tests. Manual override does not disable safety systems. E-stop works the same in both modes. It takes immediate priority and halts all operation.

videos.title: The standards behind MoRo’s safety in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The standards behind MoRo’s safety. MoRo’s safety is engineered to recognized standards. Not ad-hoc caution. ISO 3691-4: safety requirements for industrial trucks. ANSI B56.5: safety for guided industrial vehicles. You need not memorize them. Behavior around people follows requirements, not promises.

videos.title: If MoRo does something unexpected in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: If MoRo does something unexpected. It moves somewhere new, or stops for no clear reason. If there is any immediate concern, press E-stop. Then report it. Diagnosing is not the operator’s job at this level. Report early, even if it turns out minor.

videos.title: Working alongside MoRo in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Working alongside MoRo, in 30 seconds. Give MoRo room to finish its path. Do not assume its route stays the same each day. Move with clear, steady intent. Hesitating at the edge of its path can make it slow or pause. Do not squeeze past it, or rest items on it. Treat it like any moving industrial equipment.

videos.title: A mission in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: A mission, in 30 seconds. A mission is one defined task. It has a clear origin, destination and completion condition. Before assigning, check MoRo is ready. And that the path is clear. Then supervise: steady and on time is normal. An unexpected pause is your signal. Run any new or modified mission once, under supervision. If it fails: note, assess, escalate if unclear.

videos.title: Five ways MoRo carries in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Five ways MoRo carries, in 30 seconds. MoRo supports five payload configurations. Conveyor, cobot interface and towing. Lifting, and lift-and-rotate. Each suits a different material handling need. The configuration changes what you check. Before a transfer: secure and correctly configured.

videos.title: The handshake in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The handshake, in 30 seconds. When MoRo delivers to a machine, they must coordinate. Their exchange of signals is called a handshake. Signals confirm both sides are ready. Then that the handoff is complete. And they report any error state. If the exchange pauses and does not progress: stalled. Recognize a stalled handshake and flag it.

videos.title: Power and charging in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Power and charging, in 30 seconds. All MoRo models use LFP batteries. LFP is stable, long-lasting and fine with partial charges. MoRo is rated for 8 hours of runtime. The same on all three models. It charges wirelessly in under 1 hour. Charging needs MoRo to align correctly with the dock. On screen at the end: Next: charging dock alignment. MoRo Academy, DiFacto Robotics & Automation.

videos.title: Many robots, one floor in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: From One Unit to a Fleet
videos.transcript: Many robots, one floor, in 30 seconds. More units move more material: throughput. Or keep work going if one is down: redundancy. The fleet system coordinates units to avoid collisions. Zones: shared paths and reserved routes. A deadlock is two or more units waiting on each other. Designed to resolve it, typically by rerouting one unit.

videos.title: When something goes wrong in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: When something goes wrong, in 30 seconds. At L2 you recognize, categorize and know when to escalate. You do not attempt the fix. Ask: what was MoRo doing just before? What does its status show now? Has anything changed around it? Share those details when you escalate.

videos.title: Conditions and loops in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Conditions and loops, in 30 seconds. A mission can include conditional logic. If a condition is met, take one path; otherwise, another. It can also repeat: a loop. A loop continues until a defined end state. One mission definition can cover more situations.

videos.title: Three kinds of maintenance in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Three kinds of maintenance, in 30 seconds. Preventive: scheduled work, whatever the condition. Predictive: triggered by signs of degradation. Corrective: fixing something after it has failed. A mature program relies primarily on preventive and predictive. Corrective is the exception.

videos.title: Time and usage in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Setting maintenance intervals, in 30 seconds. Intervals are set from time elapsed and actual usage. Usage means operating hours and cycles completed. A heavily used unit may need attention sooner. Both count together, not either one alone. Specific intervals: to be confirmed against DiFacto documentation.

videos.title: Predictive or preventive in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Predictive or preventive? Preventive maintenance follows a set schedule. It runs regardless of condition. Predictive acts on actual signs of degradation. A component wearing faster than typical. A metric drifting from its normal range. That takes closer, ongoing observation.

videos.title: Handling a battery safely in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Handling a battery safely. LFP is generally safer than many lithium chemistries. It still needs care. Lockout and tagout before any physical battery work. Watch for damage, unusual heat or swelling. Those go beyond routine replacement. Escalate immediately; do not keep handling.

videos.title: Symptom or root cause in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Symptom or root cause? A symptom: MoRo stops repeatedly in one area. A root cause: a specific sensor, map or mechanical issue. Treat only the symptom, and it comes back. First, confirm the symptom is reproducible. Then isolate which subsystem is implicated. Narrow it down with the fault code tree and the interface.

videos.title: How a decision tree works in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: How a Decision Tree Is Structured
videos.transcript: A decision tree, in 30 seconds. It starts with a broad symptom category. Each question branches the path. Each answer narrows toward a likely cause. Answer each branch honestly, from what you observe. Do not skip ahead to a cause that seems likely.

videos.title: Safety under pressure in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Safety under pressure. Time pressure never justifies skipping safety. Lockout and tagout before physical maintenance work. Proper E-stop use during testing. Careful handling around powered systems. A correct fix that bypasses safety does not pass.

videos.title: A programmed mission in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: A programmed mission, in 30 seconds. It is built from waypoints on the map. Waypoints are specific locations. Connected by a defined sequence. Conditional logic adds more complex behavior. You define the structure yourself, explicitly.

videos.title: A good mapping pass in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: A good mapping pass, in 30 seconds. Map the space as it normally is. Typical equipment positions, no unusual obstructions. Guide MoRo through the space methodically. Cover every area it will need to navigate. Go at a deliberate pace, not a rushed one. LiDAR then builds an accurate picture as it goes.

videos.title: Do you need a zone in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Do you need a zone? In 30 seconds. Start with the facility’s real traffic patterns. Where is fleet density high? Where would several units in a narrow passage be a problem? Which routes are time-sensitive and need priority? Not every facility needs extensive zoning. Light traffic may need only minimal zones.

videos.title: Testing a handshake in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Testing a handshake, in 30 seconds. Signals must reach the right I/O points. A wrong I/O point can make it unreliable or fail. Even when both systems work fine. Test through many complete cycles, not just one. An intermittent failure points to timing or setup. One good test would have missed it.

videos.title: Read and control: the MoRo API in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The MoRo API, in 30 seconds. Read access pulls data out. Fleet status, mission history, unit health. Control access pushes commands in. It can assign missions and trigger actions. A request can move physical equipment. So only authorized systems should have control access.

videos.title: Commissioning a new site in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: The Capstone of the Programmer Track
videos.transcript: Commissioning a new site, in 30 seconds. First, assess the site: layout, clearances, network, safety. Then build the map, ideally in a quiet period. Program the core missions first, starting narrow. Validate each integration, repeatedly and under realistic variation. Go-live is not the end: hand over to the operators. Document the map version, missions and integrations.

videos.title: Where MoRo plugs into the factory in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Where MoRo plugs into the factory. Fixed machines: a request, ready, complete handshake. OPC-UA: data out to SCADA. MES and WMS APIs: orders in, reports out. A custom REST API: bespoke, application-specific needs. Example: the MES sends a production order. MoRo does the move; status goes to SCADA.

videos.title: From production event to mission in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: From production event to mission. The MES records a production run as complete. That event can trigger a MoRo mission automatically. Or the WMS records a new order to fulfill. That can start a pick operation. No operator has to assign each mission by hand.

videos.title: OPC-UA or a custom API in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: When OPC-UA Versus Custom API Makes Sense
videos.transcript: OPC-UA or a custom API? OPC-UA suits established industrial systems. Such as SCADA and many PLC platforms. They natively expect it. A custom REST API suits bespoke needs. A custom dashboard, an unusual report. Choose by what the receiving system expects.

videos.title: Performance levels in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Performance levels, in 30 seconds. EN ISO 13849 defines performance levels. They set how reliably a safety function must perform. The level comes from a risk assessment of the hazard. Higher risk needs a higher performance level. That means more robust, often redundant, design. MoRo cell levels: to be confirmed with DiFacto.

videos.title: How many robots in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: How many robots? In 30 seconds. Fleet size depends on three things. Throughput: how much moves, and how fast. Space: more units need more room. Redundancy: can the cell lose a unit? Oversize, and capital is wasted. Undersize, and throughput bottlenecks. Model real demand; do not guess.

videos.title: Standardize or customize in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Standardize or customize? In 30 seconds. Fully standardized: identical everywhere. Easier to maintain and train for. But it may not fit every site. Full customization fits each site better. But sites diverge: a long-term maintenance burden. Standardize where it serves; adapt where it is worth it.

videos.title: The machine tending cycle in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The machine tending cycle, in 30 seconds. MoRo delivers raw material to the CNC machine. A handshake confirms the machine is ready. The CNC completes its machining operation. MoRo retrieves the finished part. Then it delivers the next raw material. The cycle repeats, so handshake reliability matters.

videos.title: Complex workflows in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Complex workflows, in 30 seconds. Simple handoffs suffice for straightforward cases. Complex ones coordinate multiple machines. Through shared PLC logic. Or route by part type or production schedule. That means working inside the PLC logic itself.

videos.title: Lift and rotate in 30 seconds
videos.sectionTitle: Mechanics of Combined Lift and Rotation
videos.transcript: Lift and rotate, in 30 seconds. The load has two degrees of freedom. Vertical position: how high it is lifted. Rotational orientation: how far it turns. Stability depends on both together. It changes continuously as height and angle shift. This adds to the center-of-gravity considerations.

videos.title: Measuring the impact in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Measuring optimization impact. Measure against the same metrics you started with. Throughput or cycle time, before and after. Use consistent data for both. Do not assume it improved because it seemed logical. Real comparison beats well-intentioned guessing.

videos.title: The capstone project in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: The capstone project, in 30 seconds. A real, substantial project, not a quiz. It brings together the whole L4B track. Skills shown through actual work. Reviewed by peers against a structured rubric. Design, build, testing and documentation. Working but poorly documented does not meet the bar.

videos.title: How adults learn in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: How adults learn technical skills. Adults engage best with practical relevance. Why does this matter for my actual job? That question beats abstract theory for its own sake. This curriculum uses real-world, role-specific content. Know why the approach works, not just the pattern. Then you can teach it well.

videos.title: A valid assessment in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: What makes an assessment valid? It measures the competency it claims to measure. Failure mode: testing recall when you need skill. Or the reverse: testing skill when recall is the goal. Written alone cannot validate hands-on skill. Practical alone does not confirm understanding. So this curriculum pairs both, from L2 up.

videos.title: Handshake timing in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Teaching an integrated system. Learners often struggle most with handshake timing. MoRo and FANUC each wait for the other’s signal. They do not act independently. Address the confusion early. Build on the handshake from L3B-M4.

videos.title: Minimum lab requirements in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Minimum lab requirements, in 30 seconds. For L2 and above: a MoRo unit. The A-500 is proposed as the primary training unit, to be confirmed. ANT Server and Wi-Fi for fleet communication. Clear floor space and a payload fixture. Safety barriers or pedestrian markings. L3A and above add tools, spares, VLAN switching and FANUC access.

videos.title: Debriefing after a session in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Debriefing after a session. Start with the new instructor’s own view. What went well? What would they adjust? Mentor feedback comes second. It fills gaps or confirms what they noticed. This builds their own evaluative judgment. Not dependence on feedback for every session.

videos.title: Observed delivery in 30 seconds
videos.transcript: Observed delivery, in 30 seconds. An experienced evaluator watches you teach. Senior faculty, working alongside DiFacto. A real or representative session. Not just technical accuracy: teaching skills. Structure, checking understanding, feedback, environment. An unsuccessful attempt is feedback, not final.
